messages:
alex: Heads-up: since 09:12 UTC we're seeing intermittent apiserver 503s in eu-west1. Controller-manager hit OOM/restarts twice. Correlating with a burst of GPU attach events from the provisioner.

sasha: Oof. I can see a QPS spike on apiserver around 09:11-09:13 — ~4k/s sustained. apiserver CPU at 90% and keepalive connections climbing. Conntrack table on the NAT gateway is near exhaustion.

mira: Can you paste the controller-manager logs? wondering if it's retry storms from failed Node objects.

sasha: here are snippets from controller-manager around restart:
```
E0312 09:12:34.123 controller-runtime: reconcile failed: error patching Node: "client timeout"
I0312 09:12:35.890 sync_node: retrying attach for GPU node-attach-xyz
panic: runtime: out of memory
```

alex: also saw this in apiserver healthz intermittently: `GET /healthz` returning 503, message `etcd: request timed out` at times.

sam: We recently reduced the reserved Dedicated GPU pool in eu-west1 to cut cost (monthly commit trimmed). That lowered standing capacity and made the autoscaler churn harder when a spike arrived — more attach/detach ops. Might be the root cause.

mira: So cost optimization -> fewer idle GPUs -> attach storms -> control plane overload. Classic.

sasha: Short-term mitigation: increase conntrack on NAT gateway, add a soft rate-limit in the provisioner to spread attach operations, and temporarily re-open a small warm pool (2-4 GPUs) to absorb bursts.

sam: I can flip a temporary warm-pool flag. PR: https://github.com/redwood/provisioner/pull/402 (WIP) adding `--max-attach-per-sec` and backoff.

alex: Nice. Also open a kube-apiserver safe-config to raise `--max-requests-inflight` by 20% and increase controller-manager `--concurrent-syncs` watch a little? We should canary those changes.

mira: Agree — but raising in-flight without addressing conntrack only delays failure. Priority: NAT conntrack bump + provisioner rate-limit + warm pool.

sasha: On NAT side I've requested a config increase with networking; they replied ETA 25m. In the meantime, I'm pushing a small change to provisioner to cap attach concurrency to 6/s.

sam: Rolling temp warm pool now (eu-west1), adding 3 GPUs, tagging as warm-pool:temp-attach-mitigation.

infra-bot: Incident created INC-20260321-171666 (severity: high) — auto-detected apiserver 503 spike in eu-west1.

alex: Thanks. Action items: @sasha - deploy provisioner cap and monitor attach rate, @sam - confirm warm pool live and audit costs, @mira - file postmortem template and include cost/decision timeline. I'll draft the canary plan for apiserver/controller-manager config.

sasha: provisioner cap is deployed to staging; rolling to eu-west1 now. Monitoring dashboard updated: `provisioner.attach_rate`, `apiserver.qps`, `conntrack_usage`.

sam: warm pool is live. ETA for scale stabilization ~ 4m. cost impact: ~+$120/day while active.

mira: created postmortem stub: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1987, added initial timeline and owners.

alex: Early signal: attach rate dropped from ~30/s to ~5-6/s, apiserver QPS down to 1.1k/s, conntrack count stabilized below threshold. Controller-manager restarts stopped.

sasha: monitoring shows apiserver CPU back to ~45% and keepalive spikes cleared. I'll leave the provisioner cap in place for 2 hours while we watch.

sam: leaving warm pool for 6 hours, then we'll evaluate whether to keep it as a small reserved capacity or implement a cheaper pre-warmed option.

mira: Postmortem owners assigned, timeline + cost analysis section populated. We should add a follow-up to bake provisioner rate-limiting into autoscaler decisions (so cost changes don't cause control-plane storms).

alex: Agreed. Follow-ups: 1) permanent provisioner rate-limit PR + tests, 2) autoscaler policy change to keep minimal warm capacity based on SLOs (not cost), 3) revisit NAT sizing for eu-west1.

infra-bot: Incident INC-20260321-171666 updated: mitigations applied, monitoring OK; next update in 1h or on status change.

alex: Good job team. We'll leave this thread open until we decide on permanent config. :thumbsup:
